title: Women and survivors march in Delhi to pledge against child marriage

tea.why: Participants marched to advocate for the eradication of child marriage and to raise awareness on the eve of the International Day for the Elimination of…
tea.want: The participants pledged to end child marriage by 2030 and committed to reporting instances of the practice to the authorities.

summary: On November 26, 2026, a torchlight procession and awareness march took place at Kusumpur Pahari in Delhi to advocate for the elimination of child marriage. Organised by the civil society network Just Rights for Children, the event brought together approximately 2,000 women, children, survivors of child marriage, and local residents. Union Minister of State for Women and Child Development Savitri Thakur led the march and administered an oath to participants, pledging to prevent child marriage and report cases to the authorities. The event was held to mark Constitution Day and precede the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. Speakers highlighted the government's Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat campaign and discussed the socio-economic impacts of child marriage, while survivors shared personal accounts of resisting the practice.
